name: Western Wall
description: The holiest site in Judaism, a 2,000-year-old limestone retaining wall in Jerusalem's Old City where millions come to pray.

name: Masada
description: An ancient fortress atop a sheer desert plateau overlooking the Dead Sea, site of the last Jewish stand against Rome in 73 CE.

name: Dead Sea Shore
description: The shores of the world's saltiest natural lake, located at the lowest point on Earth at 430 m below sea level, famous for its buoyant waters.

name: Sea of Galilee
description: Israel's largest freshwater lake and the lowest freshwater lake on Earth, revered in Christianity as the site of many of Jesus's miracles.

name: Ramon Crater
description: The world's largest erosion crater, stretching 40 km long and 500 m deep in the heart of the Negev Desert, a geological wonder rich in fossils and unique wildlife.

name: Jaffa Old City
description: One of the oldest port cities in the world with a history spanning 7,500 years, featuring a picturesque harbor, ancient ruins, and a thriving artists' quarter adjacent to Tel Aviv.

name: Coral Beach Reserve
description: A protected marine reserve on the Red Sea in Eilat, home to one of the world's northernmost coral reef ecosystems with over 1,000 species of fish and coral.

name: Dome of the Rock
description: A 7th-century Islamic shrine on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem, recognized by its stunning golden dome and intricate mosaics.

name: Baha'i Gardens Haifa
description: Nineteen terraced gardens cascading down the slopes of Mount Carmel in Haifa, surrounding the gilded shrine of the Báb.

name: Caesarea
description: An ancient port city built by Herod the Great featuring a well-preserved Roman amphitheater, aqueduct, and harbor ruins along the Mediterranean coast.

name: Acre Old City
description: A UNESCO World Heritage walled city with Crusader-era halls, Ottoman bazaars, and a dramatic sea fortress on the northern coast.

name: Rosh Hanikra
description: Dramatic white chalk cliffs on Israel's northern Mediterranean coast, honeycombed by sea-carved grottos accessible by cable car at the Lebanese border.

name: Beit She'an Ruins
description: One of the best-preserved Roman-Byzantine cities in the Middle East, with colonnaded streets, a massive theater, and bathhouses excavated in the Jordan Valley.

name: Mount of Olives
description: A ridge east of Jerusalem's Old City with a panoramic view over the Temple Mount, dotted with ancient olive groves and thousands of years of Jewish burial sites.

name: Ein Gedi Nature Reserve
description: A lush desert oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, with freshwater springs, waterfalls, and rich wildlife including ibex and hyrax amid arid canyon landscapes.

name: Tel Dan Sanctuary
description: An ancient Canaanite and Israelite city in northern Israel near the source of the Jordan River, with an exceptionally preserved arched gate dating to 1750 BCE.

name: Yad Vashem
description: Israel's official memorial to the six million Jewish victims of the Holocaust, set on the Mount of Remembrance in Jerusalem.

name: Timna Park
description: A geological reserve in the southern Negev featuring dramatic red sandstone formations, ancient Egyptian temples, and copper mines over 6,000 years old.

name: Tel Megiddo
description: An archaeological site in the Jezreel Valley preserving 26 layers of ancient civilizations, including Canaanite temples and Israelite palaces, linked to the biblical Armageddon.

name: Nimrod Fortress
description: A massive Crusader and Mamluk castle on a ridge overlooking the Golan Heights, one of the largest and best-preserved medieval fortresses in the Middle East.

name: Ben-Gurion's Tomb
description: The simple desert grave of Israel's founding father David Ben-Gurion at Sde Boker, overlooking the dramatic Zin Valley and the Negev wilderness he chose for retirement.

name: Beit Alpha Synagogue
description: A 6th-century Byzantine-era synagogue in the Jezreel Valley with a stunning mosaic floor depicting a zodiac wheel and biblical scenes, a masterpiece of ancient Jewish art.

name: Latrun
description: A strategic hilltop between Jerusalem and Tel Aviv, home to a Trappist monastery, a British-era fort, and Israel's national armored corps museum amid ancient terraced vineyards.

name: Gamla Nature Reserve
description: An ancient Jewish city in the Golan Heights that staged a heroic revolt against Rome in 67 CE, now a reserve with dramatic basalt ruins, a waterfall, and nesting griffon vultures.

name: Church of Holy Sepulchre
description: The holiest site in Christianity in Jerusalem's Old City, built over the sites of Jesus's crucifixion, burial, and resurrection, drawing pilgrims from across the world.
